questions.q:
Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words.

Arteries : Circulatory system
questions.solution:
The relation is:

Arteries : Circulatory system

Arteries – vessel that carries blood high in oxygen content away from the heart to the farthest reaches of the body. Since blood in arteries is usually full of oxygen, the haemoglobin in the red blood cells is oxygenated.

Circulatory system – The system that circulates blood and lymph through the body, consisting of the heart, blood vessels, blood, lymph, and the lymphatic vessels and glands.

So, the relation is that arteries forms the Circulatory system of our body.

1) Kidney : Respiratory system

Kidney – The kidneys are two bean-shaped organs in the renal system. They help the body pass waste as urine. They also help filter blood before sending it back to the heart, creating hormones that help produce red blood cells, promote bone health, and regulate blood pressure.

Respiratory system – The human respiratory system is a series of organs responsible for taking in oxygen and expelling carbon dioxide. The primary organs of the respiratory system are the lungs, which carry out this exchange of gases as we breathe.

The kidneys forms the excretory system of our body and not the Respiratory system.

2) Eyes : Endocrine system

Eyes – Eyes are organs of the visual system. They provide animals with vision, the ability to receive and process visual detail, as well as enabling several photo response functions that are independent of vision. Eyes detect light and convert it into electro-chemical impulses in neurons.

Endocrine system - The endocrine system is the collection of glands that produce hormones that regulate metabolism, growth and development, tissue function, sexual function, reproduction, sleep, and mood, among other things.

Eyes belong to the sensory system and not the endocrine system.

3) Lungs : Olfactory system

Lungs – The lungs are a pair of spongy, air-filled organs located on either side of the chest (thorax). The trachea (windpipe) conducts inhaled air into the lungs through its tubular branches, called bronchi. The lungs are covered by a thin tissue layer called the pleura.

Olfactory system – The olfactory system, or sense of smell, is the sensory system used for smelling (olfaction). Olfaction is one of the special senses, that have directly associated specific organs. Most mammals and reptiles have a main olfactory system and an accessory olfactory system.

Lungs are related to respiratory system, and not olfactory system.

4) Nerves : Nervous system

Nerves – Bundles of fibres or axons, in the peripheral nervous system are called nerves, and bundles of afferent fibers are known as sensory nerves. An efferent nerve fiber conducts signals from a motor neuron in the central nervous system to muscles.

Nervous system – The nervous system is a highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body. The nervous system detects environmental changes that impact the body, then works in tandem with the endocrine system to respond to such events.

The nerves forms the nervous system.

Hence, ‘Nerves : Nervous system’ is the correct answer.

questions.q:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, which of the given conclusions logically(s) follow. From the statements.

Statements:

1. Some bottles are glasses.

2. Some glasses are bowls.

Conclusions:

I. Some bowls are bottles.

II. Some glasses are bottles

III. No bowl is a bottle
options: All Conclusions I, II and III follow.
Only Conclusions II and III follow.
Either Conclusion II or III follows.
Only Conclusions II and either Conclusion I or III follow.
questions.solution:
Concept:

1) We have to check the conclusions are 100% match with the statement. If the conclusion is 100% match with the given statement then the conclusion is true. If there is a 1% chance of not following the statement then the conclusion is considered to be false.

2) The possibility case can be considered to be "false" in "definite case".

3) In Possibility case, either "can" or "possible" word must be present.

The least possible venn diagram is:



I. Some bowls are bottles. → False (It can be possible, but it is not definite)

II. Some glasses are bottles → True (It is definite)

III. No bowl is a bottle → False (It can be possible, but it is not definite)

Conclusion I and III forms a complementary pair.

Hence, only Conclusions II and either Conclusion I or III follow.

Note:

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. The elements should be the same in both the statements.

2. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

3. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

The two complementary pairs are:

1) All + Some not

2) No + Some

questions.solution:

• Argon improves bulb life by avoiding too rapid a degradation of the tungsten filaments.

• Nitrogen also added in incandescent light bulbs at the rate of 7%.

• Argon has a comparable low breakdown voltage, applying a small amount of nitrogen to avoid arcing between the supports of the filaments.

• Other gasses like hydrogen, neon, nitrogen and krypton are also used for illumination purposes.

• High-brightness "halogen" bulbs use argon mixture and a limited quantity of halogen, usually bromine or iodine.

questions.q: In a circle, AB is the diameter and CD is a chord. AB and CD produced meet at a point P, outside the circle. If PD = 15.3 cm, CD = 11.9 cm and AP = 30.6 cm, then the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
PC = PD + CD = 15.3 + 11.9 = 27.2

AP × PB = PD × PC

⇒ 30.6 × PB = 15.3 × 27.2

⇒ PB = (15.3 × 27.2)/30.6

⇒ PB = 13.6

Now, AB = AP - PB = 30.6 - 13.6 = 17 cm

Radius of the circle = 17/2 = 8.5 cm

questions.q: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 575 km, A train starts from station ‘A’ at 3.00 p.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 50 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 3.30 p.m and moves towards station ‘A’ at an average speed of 60 km/h, how far from station ‘A’ will the trains meet?
questions.solution:
The distance between two stations, A and B = 575 km,

Speed of first train = 50 km/hr

Speed of second train = 60 km/hr

Distance covered by first train in 30 min (1/2 hr) = 50 × 1/2 = 25 km

Remaining distance = 575 - 25 = 550 km

Relative speed, if opposite direction = 50 + 60 = 110 km/hr

As we know,

Time = Distance/speed

Both train meet each other in = 550/110 = 5 hrs

Distance covered in 5 hrs by first train = 5 × 50 = 250 km

Total distance covered by first train = 25 + 250 = 275 km

Both trains meet each other 275 km far from station A.

questions.q:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Johnny’s mother said, “Johnny, run down to the grocer’s and get a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.”
options: Johnny’s mother asked him to run down to the grocer’s and get a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.
Johnny commanded his mother to go down to the grocer and buy a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.
Johnny’s mother pleaded with John to run down to the grocer’s and get her a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.
Johnny asked his mother to run down to the grocer’s and get a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., Johnny’s mother asked him to run down to the grocer’s and get a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.

Key Points

• The sentence seems like a command given by the mother to Johnny; but it is, in fact, an errand or task that Johnny's mother has 'asked him to do'.

• So, when turning the sentence into indirect, the verb 'asked' is more appropriate here than 'commanded' or 'pleaded'..

• In the indirect form, the reporting verb "said" changes to "asked," and the noun "Johnny" changes to "him" as the subject becomes the object.

• Also, the imperative verb "run" is changed to its infinitive forms "to run".

• The tense of the reported verb remains the same as in the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence by making Johnny the subject who is commanding his mother to go down to the grocer and buy the items, which is the opposite of what is intended.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it changes the reporting verb to "pleaded," which implies a request made with desperation or urgency. The original sentence does not convey any such urgency or desperation.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it changes the roles of the speaker and the listener. In the original sentence, Johnny’s mother is the speaker who is making the request, while Johnny is the listener. However, in option 4, Johnny becomes the speaker, asking his mother to go to the grocer, which is the opposite of the intended meaning.

So, the indirect sentence becomes: *Johnny’s mother asked him to run down to the grocer’s and get a loaf of French bread and a pound of cheddar cheese.*
